login.title: Welcome back
login.subtitle: Continue where you left off. Your checklist, messages and deadlines are waiting.

aside.eyebrow: Study in Korea, step by step
aside.title: One calm place for every step to a Korean university.
aside.text: From your first search to the day you land at Incheon, Hangyul Univ shows you what to do next, and why.
aside.point1: See which programs fit you, with clear reasons for each.
aside.point2: Keep every document in one secure vault and reuse it across applications.
aside.point3: Prepare with real people on the Hangyul team who speak your language.
aside.note: Thousands of small steps, one clear next step at a time.

register.title: Create your account
register.subtitle: Four short steps. We verify your email and mobile number so your account and your documents stay yours.
register.fromCheck: Your answers are saved to your profile, so your matches are ready as soon as you sign up.
register.nationalityHint: Your nationality decides which documents and visa steps apply to you.
register.phoneHint: We send a one-time code by text message. Standard rates may apply.
register.passwordHint: At least 10 characters. A sentence you will remember works best.
register.exists: An account with this email already exists. Try signing in instead.
register.privacyNote: Your documents and personal details are shared only with the Hangyul team that supports you (including its partner agency) and the universities you choose. You can export or delete your data at any time.

verify.title: Verify your contact details
verify.text: Enter the codes we sent. Each code works for 5 minutes.
verify.consoleHint: Development: codes are not delivered. Use the development tools to read them.
verify.expired: That code expired. Request a new one.
verify.tooMany: Too many incorrect codes. Request a new one.
verify.deliveryFailedEmail: We could not send the email. Please try again.
verify.deliveryFailedSms: We could not send the text message. Please try again.
verify.tooSoon: Please wait a moment before requesting another code.
verify.limited: Too many requests. Please try again later.

UNREACHABLE.email: We couldn't reach our email service just now. Everything you entered is saved. Try again in {{seconds}} seconds.
UNREACHABLE.sms: We couldn't reach our text message service just now. Everything you entered is saved. Try again in {{seconds}} seconds.

RECIPIENT_INVALID.email: We can't send email to this address. Please check it.
RECIPIENT_INVALID.sms: We can't text this number. Please check the country code and mobile number.

REGION_UNSUPPORTED.email: We can't send email to this address. Please use another email address.
REGION_UNSUPPORTED.sms: We can't send texts to numbers in this country yet. Use another mobile number or write to support@talkhangyul.com.

RECIPIENT_REJECTED.email: The receiving mail server refused our email. Please use another address.
RECIPIENT_REJECTED.sms: This number is blocking our texts. Unblock them or use another number.

RECIPIENT_UNREACHABLE.email: The email didn't get through. Please try again shortly.
RECIPIENT_UNREACHABLE.sms: Your phone seems to be off or out of coverage. Check it and try again.

SERVICE_CONFIG.sms: Something is wrong with our text messages. Everything you entered is saved. Try again in {{seconds}} seconds.

consent.title: How we handle your information
consent.text: Required items are needed to open an account. You can withdraw optional consent at any time in Settings.

TERMS.label: I agree to the Terms of Service

PRIVACY.label: I agree to the collection and use of my personal information
PRIVACY.summary: Email, mobile number, name, nationality and password (stored encrypted), to create and protect your account.

CROSS_BORDER_VERIFICATION.label: I acknowledge that my email and mobile number are processed abroad to verify them
CROSS_BORDER_VERIFICATION.summary: Twilio Inc. (United States) delivers the verification text and email; Cloudflare, Inc. (United States) checks that sign-up is not automated. Details, including how to refuse, are in the Privacy Policy. Refusing means an account cannot be created.

MARKETING.label: Send me study-in-Korea news and event information
MARKETING.summary: Optional. By email or text; unsubscribe any time.

consent.canonical: The Korean text is the legally binding version; this translation is for your convenience.
consent.missing: Please agree to the required items.

tierText.STRONG: You meet the published requirements comfortably and these programs match your preferences.
tierText.COMPETITIVE: You meet the requirements, but other factors (grades, budget, timing) make it less certain.

method.title: How matching works
method.stage1: Stage 1: Eligibility. We check each program's published entry requirements (education level, grades, TOPIK or English, deadlines, nationality rules).
method.stage2: Stage 2: Fit. Eligible programs are ranked by named, weighted factors such as field, budget, scholarships, location and housing. Open any card to see the points.
method.noProbability: We never estimate your chance of admission. Tiers describe how well you meet published criteria, not what a university will decide.

guarantee.title: Partner admission guarantee

legalFlow.title: How to get it accepted in Korea: {{path}}

intro.APOSTILLE: {{country}} is part of the Apostille Convention, so one apostille replaces embassy legalization. Only these steps apply to you.
intro.CONSULAR_LEGALIZATION: {{country}} is not part of the Apostille Convention, so the document is legalized in two stages: first by your government, then by the Korean embassy.
intro.ISSUER_VERIFICATION: The issuer verifies this document directly. Only these steps apply to you.

legalFlow.onlyIfRequired: only if the issuer requires it

original.where: The school or authority that issued it
original.why: Korean universities only accept originals or certified copies.
original.title: Get the official original (or a certified copy) from the issuer

notarize.why: Some authorities apostille or legalize only notarized copies.
notarize.title: Notarize the copy if the issuing authority requires it

apostille.where: The apostille authority in {{country}} (usually the foreign or justice ministry)
apostille.why: It proves to Korea that the document is genuine. No embassy visit is needed.
apostille.title: Get an apostille from the competent authority in {{country}}

mofa.where: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs in {{country}}
mofa.why: Your government confirms the issuer's signature and seal first.
mofa.title: Authenticate it at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of {{country}}

consular.where: The Korean embassy or consulate in {{country}}
consular.why: The Korean embassy then confirms your ministry's stamp, so Korean universities accept it.
consular.title: Get consular legalization at the Korean embassy or consulate in {{country}}

chsi.why: Many Korean universities ask Chinese applicants for this official degree verification report.
chsi.title: Get the CHSI / CDGDC verification report

translation.where: A certified translator (or a translation notarized in {{country}})
translation.why: Universities read Korean or English; other languages need a certified translation.
translation.title: Certified translation into Korean or English if the document is in another language

verify.why: The Hangyul team checks it once, and it is reused for every application.
verify.title: Upload it for Hangyul verification

note.JOINS: {{country}} joins the Apostille Convention on {{date}}. Until then, documents need Korean consular legalization.
note.JOINED: {{country}} joined the Apostille Convention on {{date}}. Documents legalized by the consulate before that date are generally still accepted. Confirm with your university.
note.UNVERIFIED: We have not verified the legalization route for this country yet. The Hangyul team will confirm.

payee.EVERYDAY: Food, transport and phone, paid as you go

when.BEFORE_VISA: Before you apply for your visa

note.TUITION_PER_SEMESTER: Paid each semester; the first by the tuition deadline.
note.DORM_PER_SEMESTER: Paid each semester; vacation stays are usually extra.
note.VISA_FEE_ROUTE: From the embassy's published fee for your route.
note.VISA_FEE_PARTIAL: From the embassy's page; some details of this route are still being checked.
note.VISA_FEE_AS_PUBLISHED: The embassy publishes this fee in words. See the official wording.
note.VISA_FEE_UNKNOWN: Not published for your route yet. The Hangyul team confirms.
note.VISA_FEE_NO_ROUTE: We haven't checked your embassy yet. The Hangyul team confirms.
note.RESIDENCE_CARD_90_DAYS: For stays over 90 days. Apply within 90 days of arrival.
note.NHIS_D2: About this much per month, based on 2026 university notices (NHIS does not publish it). Starts when you apply for your residence card.
note.NHIS_D4: About this much per month (2026, university notices). For language students it starts 6 months after entry; many Korean language institutes require group insurance before that.
note.HANGYUL_FEE_NONE: Optional. Only if you choose a Hangyul plan.
note.VISA_FEE_FREE: Your nationality is exempt in the embassy's fee table.

funds.title: Money you must show (not pay)
funds.sub: For the {{type}} visa, the embassy asks to see this money in the bank. It is not paid to anyone, but it must really be yours or your family's.

amount.CAPITAL: {{amount}} for a university in Seoul, Gyeonggi or Incheon
amount.OTHER: {{amount}} for a university outside the Seoul area

kind.PER_ADMISSION_CERTIFICATE: The amount written on your admission certificate (one year of tuition and living costs)
kind.NOT_STATED: The embassy states no minimum amount. Plan for one year of tuition and living costs; the Hangyul team confirms.

period.HELD_one: Kept in the account for at least {{count}} month
period.HELD_other: Kept in the account for at least {{count}} months
period.HISTORY_one: Bank statement for the last {{count}} month
period.HISTORY_other: Bank statements for the last {{count}} months

funds.periodDays_one: Kept in the account for at least {{count}} day
funds.periodDays_other: Kept in the account for at least {{count}} days
funds.longer_one: {{count}} month if your university is in the lower tier (rated 'consulting' by the government)
funds.longer_other: {{count}} months if your university is in the lower tier (rated 'consulting' by the government)

whose.OWN_NAME: In the student's own name (parents' income papers may also be asked)
whose.STUDENT_OR_PARENT: In the student's or a parent's name (a parent's account needs a family relationship certificate)
whose.UNKNOWN: Whose name: the Hangyul team confirms with the embassy

funds.certAge_one: Certificate issued at most {{count}} day before you apply
funds.certAge_other: Certificate issued at most {{count}} days before you apply
funds.waived: Your university is in the top ('excellent') tier, so the embassy may not ask for this. The Hangyul team confirms.
funds.genuine: The money must actually be in the account. Putting money in only to get a certificate and then taking it out is illegal in Korea.

status.NO_ROUTE: We haven't checked the money rule for your embassy yet. The Hangyul team confirms it.
status.NEEDS_PROFILE: Add your nationality and what you want to study to see the money rule for your visa.

guard.title: Pay tuition safely
guard.text: Pay the university directly, by bank transfer or the payment method the university lists, in the student's own name. Don't pay through money changers, agencies or anyone else's account: the university's account can be frozen, and refunds go only to the student's own account.

announced.title_one: {{count}} change announced, not in force yet
announced.title_other: {{count}} changes announced, not in force yet

rule.TOPIK4_FINANCIAL_EXEMPTION: Students with TOPIK level 4 (or KIIP level 4) would not need to show funds for the visa.
rule.STUDY_DEPOSIT_SCHEME: Students from some countries without a Korean test result would deposit study funds in a bank, paid out each semester.
rule.REFUND_TO_STUDENT_ACCOUNT: After a visa refusal, tuition would be refunded directly to an account in the student's name (standard agreement).
